text:
alex: heads up — after this morning's rollout i'm seeing a p95 latency regression on the small T4 pools :eyes:. attaching profiler snippets and quick logs. anyone else seeing a spike?

chris: seeing it too on canary. looks correlated with high batch-formation times for short seq requests.

maria: can you paste the flame/stack?

alex: pasted below. this is a 5-minute sample during the spike.
```
kernel_selector.choose() -> generic_kernel fallback ++
queue.form_window_ms: 22 -> effective 45 under contention
kv_cache.evictions/5m: 1123
token_budget.current_alloc: 8 -> steal events ++
prefill.enqueue_latency_p95: 18ms
decode.enqueue_latency_p95: 46ms
overall p95 latency: 420ms
```

chris: interesting that decode enqueue p95 is high while prefill is fine. suggests queue head-of-line blocking when long-running batches form.

jonathan: could be our continuous-batching heuristic. if batch_window expands when small requests arrive behind large ones we penalize short decodes.

maria: i prototyped splitting queues into "seed" (init/prefill) vs "stream" (decode) locally. two queues, separate token_budget targets. results looked promising on a microbench.

alex: can you share numbers?

maria: sure — microbench (phi-7b, T4 small) single-tenant:
```
baseline (single queue): p95 overall 420ms, p95 decode 460ms, kernel fallback rate 8.6%
queue-split (seed+stream): p95 overall 310ms, p95 decode 240ms, kernel fallback rate 1.9%
```

chris: huge delta. what config changes did you make?

maria: minimal: separate token budgets and smaller formation windows for stream queue. config snippet: 
```
queues: [
  { name: "seed", formation_ms: 30, token_budget_target: 12, prefer_kernel: "prefill_small" },
  { name: "stream", formation_ms: 8, token_budget_target: 4, prefer_kernel: "decode_light" }
]
kernel_affinity_thresholds: { decode_light: 0.6, prefill_small: 0.4 }
kv_priming_window_ms: 250
```

jonathan: i like the separate formation_ms. stream gets much shorter window so small gen requests don't wait behind large prefill batches.

alex: kernel_affinity_thresholds — explain?

maria: we bias kernel selector to prefer smaller/fast kernels for stream until confidence drops. reduces costly kernel fallbacks at short seq lengths. in the profiler we saw many requests switching to generic_kernel because batch shape didn't match optimized kernels.

chris: did you measure kernel switch count?

maria: yes. before: kernel_switches/min ~ 72, fallback hits 8.6% of gen ops. after: kernel_switches/min 18, fallback 1.9%.

alex: what about KV cache behavior? earlier log shows evictions high.

maria: eviction problem was mostly from microbatch steal/reshuffle when seed queue allowed larger token budgets. splitting queues reduced kv churn. also raising kv_priming_window_ms to 250ms helped. kv miss rate dropped from 7% -> 1.2% in microbench.

jonathan: any perf regressions introduced by split? throughput impact?

maria: small throughput drop for high-latency long-prefill workloads if you keep stream formation tiny. but net latency and tail wins are worth it for interactive use cases. we can tune token_budget_target per customer tier.

chris: we should run cluster-wide canary. i have a script to replay production sample. run command: 
```
./tools/bench/replay_workload.py --sample prod-2026-03-15 --duration 20m --variant queue-split
```

alex: ops-bot — can you spin a canary with queue-split on 3 nodes in us-west?

ops-bot: requested canary started: canary-id=c-62472-qsplit nodes=[r4-t4-small-3] owner=chris

chris: started replay now. i'm tracking p50/p95, kv_miss, kernel_fallback. will post results.

(20m later)

chris: quick canary summary: p95 went 418ms -> 312ms across canary, decode p95 445ms -> 235ms, kv_miss 6.8% -> 1.4%, kernel_fallback 7.9% -> 2.0%. no stability issues.

alex: nice. any edge cases?

maria: if a single request triggers both long prefill and immediate decode (rare), it will be split across queues and we need to ensure KV affinity keeps both halves local. we added a correlation token to avoid cross-node KV misses.

jonathan: what about batching fairness — do we starve long prefill jobs when stream floods in?

maria: we added a soft weight so seed gets at least 30% tokens in a busy period. token_budget_target per queue enforces that.

chris: plan: roll queue-split as opt-in feature flag, run for 24h on small pools, monitor tail latencies + cost delta. add dashboard panels for kernel_fallback, kv_miss, token_steal events.

alex: add an experiment to vary stream formation_ms {4,8,12} and token_budget_target {2,4,6} to find sweet spot per model class.

maria: i'll upload my microbench harness + config to /opt/bench/queue_split/ and add to repo. quick usage: 
```
python3 scripts/queue_split_bench.py --model redwood/phi-7b --n 1000 --window 8
```

chris: PR incoming with feature flag and metrics emission. cc @jonathan for rollout plan.

alex: thanks all. if canary stays stable we'll enable for low-latency tier next. file follow-ups here and paste dashboards. :thumbsup:

jonathan: noted. will schedule a short postmortem-style doc if we see any regressions.
